text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Club Mediterranee leisure group to be led by EuroDisney chairman Philippe Bourguignon.
-- Pinault-Printemps-Redoute announces executive reshuffle today, Francois-Henri Pinault to become chairman of bookstores chain FNAC.
-- Worms & Cie to absorb Saint-Louis agri-food group of which it is the majority shareholder, to rationalize holdings, according to the two companies.
-- New restructuring plan at Cie Generale des Ets Michelin puts some 1,445 jobs at risks as company seeks to improve competitivity.
-- Credit Lyonnais bailout plan to be submitted to EU authorities next month.
-- SNCF railway operator to announce 1996 loss of some 15.2 billion francs losses for 1996, some three billion more than planned which is partly due to provisioning.
-- Small and medium-sized company heads more optimistic, survey shows.
-- Difficulties met by the German government to respect the Maastricht treaty criteria cast a shadow on the implementation of a single European currency.

-- Independent supermarkets association Leclerc chairman Michel-Edouard Leclerc considers co-operation with independent chain Systeme U, seeks to intensify diversification in non-food products, lists international development as one of top priorities.
-- European Commission seeks to tax credit-card payments, as called for by retailers, but banks oppose project.
